answer: In an agent economy trading nectar, crystal, and ivory, access to paid jobs is allocated by a lottery weighted by escrowed stake, not by account count. Each stake remains locked for 30 days, and the same funds cannot back multiple accounts. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand fake agents gives no more expected work than staking 100 under one name. To gain influence, an attacker must lock up proportionally more capital and forgo its use elsewhere.
